description: Preserving Semver, plus the protective policy every consuming repo was otherwise inlining: no prereleases once a dependency is on one, a release soak matching pnpm's supply-chain setting, and rebase-when-behind.

packageRules.description: Prerelease guard. `ignoreUnstable` only blocks stable -> unstable: once a dependency is pinned to a prerelease, every later prerelease of the same line reads as an ordinary patch and flows straight through. That is the mechanism by which a type-plus 8.x beta reached eighteen published packages. This closes it from the other side: while the current version is a prerelease, only stable versions are candidates. A dependency with no stable line at all therefore stops getting update PRs (they show on the dependency dashboard); a repo that deliberately tracks a prerelease overrides this with its own packageRule, which is applied after the preset's.
